root_cause_label: Infeasible Featurization on Large Dataset Causes Infinite Timeout Loop
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wrote a featurization routine that computes all ~200 RDKit descriptors plus Morgan fingerprints for each of ~800k training molecules, causing the training script to run for over 30 minutes without completing while the agent passively monitored by issuing 18 consecutive empty commands.
t_err_evidence: create fit_model.py with per-molecule descriptor loops and deprecated Morgan fingerprint featurization over full 1M-row dataset
t_commit_evidence: At step 30 the script was launched with the correct venv and fixed split handling; it immediately began producing thousands of RDKit deprecation warnings per second (visible in terminal output) and timed out at 120s; from this point the agent only issued empty monitoring commands and never modified the approach.
t_surface_evidence: The command timed out after 120.0 seconds ... DEPRECATION WARNING: please use MorganGenerator
trigger_explanation: The agent chose a technically correct approach (RDKit descriptors + fingerprints + RandomForest) but failed to account for the computational cost: computing ~200 descriptors per molecule for 1M rows is infeasible without batching, parallelism, or feature selection. A simpler fingerprint-only approach or sampling would have been tractable. This is a code generation quality failure rather than a conceptual error.
